Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; device-list review opened</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-072</td> <td>Standing self-merge-with-full-gate authority (gh merges included)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-073">D-073</a></td> <td>D-016 device-list amendment: Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-074">D-074</a></td> <td>Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-075">D-075</a></td> <td>Extension-axis intake: ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-076">D-076</a></td> <td>Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review): measured-first budgets</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-077">D-077</a></td> <td>Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log.html#d-078">D-078</a></td> <td>Soundness gate: no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</td> <td>accepted; operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/codex-impl-round1.md:1:I could not build `scripts/spike_mlx_prompt_cache.py` because the workspace is mounted read-only and `apply_patch` was rejected by the sandbox. I did verify that `joulewise/kv_size.py` exposes clean importable helpers, so the script should prefer that path over CLI parsing. My judgment: the requested subprocess-per-stage design is genuinely airtight against accidental Python/MLX in-process state reuse because `prefill` and `decode` run in different OS processes via `sys.executable`; residual leak paths like filesystem cache, mmap cache, or OS page cache can affect timings, but not the correctness claim of token identity from serialized cache state.

docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/lens-isolation.md:3:`should-fix` [scripts/spike_mlx_prompt_cache.py](/Users/edr/code/jw-spike301/scripts/spike_mlx_prompt_cache.py:414): `run_stage()` copies the parent environment and preserves any existing `PYTHONPATH`, only prepending the repo root. That means the subprocesses are fresh OS processes, but not a sterile import/runtime environment. Concrete failure scenario: the caller has `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/mlx_lm_shadow` with a stale or patched `mlx_lm` package. All three stages import that code instead of the installed `/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/.../mlx_lm`, while `importlib.metadata.version("mlx-lm")` can still report `0.31.3`. A patched `generate_step`/cache loader could make monolithic and resumed tokens agree without proving the installed mlx-lm prompt-cache replay path. This weakens the “verified against installed source” and “only persisted cache + tokens” claim via environment-controlled code injection.
docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/lens-isolation.md:7:I found no evidence that Python globals, MLX in-process state, tokenizer objects, or the monolithic stage can cross into the decode stage on the intended `run` path. `run` invokes `monolithic`, `prefill`, and `decode` as separate `sys.executable` subprocesses, and `decode` reloads the model plus `prompt_cache.safetensors`/`prompt_tokens.json`.

The 'paged' leg is different: installed mlx-lm has NO paged/block-table cache class (the inventory is concatenate- and step-growing-buffer styles), so paged KV means either a new runtime adapter (vLLM on the 3080 Ti, NEEDS-WEB for 12 GiB feasibility) or runtime modification — not harness glue. docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/lens-evidence.md:3:- **should-fix** [scripts/spike_mlx_prompt_cache.py](/Users/edr/code/jw-spike301/scripts/spike_mlx_prompt_cache.py:480): `tokens_identical` is derived only from equality of the two generated token lists, and `verdict_for` can return `replay_supported` without checking that either list actually contains the requested 64 tokens. Equal empty lists, or equal short lists, would produce `first_divergence_index: null` and `replay_supported` at lines 447-455. The installed `generate_step` appears to yield exactly `max_tokens`, so this does not invalidate the current run outright, but the JSON artifacts only record requested `decode_tokens: 64`, not observed generated counts. That makes the doc’s `64/64` claim at [kv_feasibility.md](/Users/edr/code/jw-spike301/docs/phase_3/kv_feasibility.md:64) depend on script/runtime behavior rather than being directly recorded evidence.

I did not run MLX/model paths.
docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/codex-impl-round2.md:3:My judgment: the subprocess-per-stage design is genuinely airtight against accidental in-process state reuse because `run` invokes each stage with a fresh `sys.executable` process. Residual leak paths are OS page cache, model mmap/cache effects, filesystem cache, and possible MLX compiled-kernel caches; those can affect timings, but not the correctness claim, since the resume process reconstructs correctness only from `prompt_cache.safetensors` plus persisted prompt token IDs. I would not isolate this differently unless the goal were timing purity, in which case a reboot/container/cache-drop protocol would be relevant.

1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise: Project Status — Full Reference</h1> <p><strong><a href="project_status.html">← Back to project status summary</a></strong></p> <p>This page continues the project-status document with its architecture, planning, and historical reference material.</p> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <p>JouleWise combines a reusable, typed measurement harness with a benchmark defined by its frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. It measures the energy of LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The name nods to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement is the spine of the system; disaggregated (&quot;split&quot;) inference - running prefill and decode on different machines with the KV cache transferred between them - is the validating research study, not the whole architecture.</p> <p>The capstone now has two explicit claim tracks. The guaranteed capstone is auditable local LLM energy measurement: the harness plus the Apple-Silicon characterization it can already execute on the M3 Max. Split (disaggregated) inference remains the differentiating validating study; when Phase 3 hardware and feasibility gates land, it upgrades the capstone from local characterization to a split-energy crossover study.</p> <p>The frozen capstone headline, fallback claims, contribution ladder, and minimum-viable stop-lines are now recorded in <code>docs/contracts/capstone_scope.md</code>; that contract is the scope pointer for reader-facing wording under the claims ladder.</p> <p>The first working slice runs on a MacBook (Apple Silicon) with MLX as the runtime and <code>powermetrics</code> as the power source, producing complete, auditable run bundles. Further backends (NVIDIA + vLLM/llama.cpp, Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi + Hailo as a feasibility finding) plug into the same adapter interfaces.</p> <p>Research questions:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Q1</strong>: Under what conditions (model size, prompt length, link speed, device pair) does splitting inference reduce total energy versus running monolithically on either device?</li> <li><strong>Q2</strong>: How sensitive is the split&#39;s energy cost to interconnect bandwidth (1GbE vs 2.5GbE vs optional 10GbE) - where is the crossover?</li> <li><strong>Q3</strong>: When splitting saves energy, what latency does it cost, and vice versa (energy-latency Pareto frontier)?</li> <li><strong>Q4</strong> (added 2026-07-07, council C-003): What fixed-vs-marginal energy model <code>E = fixed + prefill(prompt_tokens) + decode(output_tokens)</code> does each target/model/quantization follow — and can split-run energy be predicted compositionally from monolithic coefficients plus transfer measurements?</li> <li><strong>Q5</strong> (C-003/C-007): On one machine, do workload/model/quantization efficiency rankings stay stable as workload shape, model, and quantization change, or where do they flip? A cross-device ranking extension is hardware-gated.</li> <li><strong>Q6</strong> (C-003; gated on the wall meter): Does the measurement boundary (platform rails vs AC wall power) change the conclusions?</li> </ul> <p>Current question status, aliases, gates, and claim ceilings live in the canonical live index, <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code>. The curated bank of further candidate questions and deliberately killed ones remains the historical/deliberative record in <code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>; the measurement noise floor / detection limit is treated as the methodology centerpiece rather than a numbered question.</p> <p>The capability map by claim ceiling is reflected in <code>docs/research_question_registry.md</code> (C-015), alongside the suite architecture v2 and benchmark interop direction; the guaranteed-capstone stop-line is recorded in the Phase 2 plan.</p> <p><strong>Q4 architectural stress-test agenda (D-070).</strong> Static batching, speculative decoding / native MTP, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning-length variance are five stress tests of Q4&#39;s single fixed-plus-marginal energy thesis, not five additional theses. The harness must instrument every axis well enough to produce strict-valid L0 smoke bundles; the benchmark supplies the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator for claim-bearing runs. Per Ed&#39;s ruling, all five axes have characterized-study commitments. Every study remains floor-gated and capped at L2; L3 is available only through Q4/AP-1&#39;s existing holdout machinery. Window A remains first, and no AXI quiet-Mac characterization starts before Window A completes. Static batching is the capstone scope; continuous batching remains a post-capstone extension.</p> <p><strong>Ranked extension-axis intake (D-075).</strong> The later six-axis evaluation did not create six more theses. It attached DSpark/DFlash break-even, proposal-work, and contamination-control riders to the speculative-decoding home; admitted an on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and one named hybrid pair; and attached cache/context, module-nonattribution, kernel, and backend provenance riders to their existing questions. All admitted units remain candidate work with earliest-phase tags, named forbidden upgrades, floor gates, and an intake ceiling at or below L2. Unverified runtime, pair, adapter, and device-fit questions remain explicitly NEEDS-WEB, and Ed retains commitment and ordering authority under D-070.</p> <h2 id="status-at-a-glance">Status At A Glance</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Phase</th> <th>Scope</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>1. Approval, feasibility, measurement design</td> <td>contracts, methodology, hardware feasibility evidence</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — the Phase 1 exit checklist owns exact completion and external gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2. Harness, Mac vertical slice, homogeneous baselines</td> <td>runnable harness, first real measurements, per-target baselines</td> <td><strong>in progress</strong> — Mac vertical slice and analysis software are implemented; remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL; the state kernel and quiet-machine rules own execution eligibility</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3. Disaggregation, KV replay, interconnect sweep</td> <td>split-energy decomposition, crossover dataset</td> <td>planned (feasibility-first)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>4. Characterization and analysis</td> <td>statistics, figures, claims audit</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> <tr> <td>5. Presentation and submission</td> <td>report, colloquium, reproducible release</td> <td>planned</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="capstone-artifact-map">Capstone Artifact Map</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>chapter/report-component</th> <th>owning doc or deliverable</th> <th>status</th> <th>missing evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Background / related work</td> <td>Phase 4 Stage 4.6, <code>docs/phase_4/related_work_draft.md</code></td> <td>drafted (11 verified sources)</td> <td>background-chapter assembly and the Phase 4 exit pass</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Measurement methodology</td> <td><code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></td> <td>complete</td> <td>Phase 4 ratification may amend statistical details against observed variance</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Harness / instrument</td> <td><code>joulewise/</code></td> <td>complete; pre-campaign software review cleared; C-028 closed</td> <td>live execution eligibility comes from the state kernel; quiet-machine work also requires Ed and the clean hardware lane</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Apple-Silicon characterization / homogeneous baselines</td> <td>Phase 2 Slice 2M, <code>docs/phase_2/baseline_results.md</code></td> <td>Window A open; production shakedown closed and first floors published; quiet-Mac execution remains</td> <td>P2-037 claim adjudication and the live state kernel govern the next baseline step; needs Ed + quiet Mac</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Split-inference study</td> <td>Phase 3</td> <td>planned</td> <td>needs KV-feasibility spikes plus a real pairing, or the synthetic-transfer + analytical-composition floor</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Results / limitations + claims audit</td> <td>Phase 4 Stages 4.3-4.5</td> <td>analysis path implemented; Window-A calibration data exist</td> <td>the floor corpus is strict-valid but claim-evidence-flagged; P2-037 adjudication must preserve the published caveats before any claim promotion</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Complete so far (all verifiable in the repository):</p> <ul> <li>A runnable harness: from a typed config, one command (<code>python3 -m joulewise run ...</code>) produces a complete, schema-valid, auditable run bundle and reduces it to energy/latency summary metrics - proven first on deterministic mock adapters (controller, bundle contract, and reducer math verified without hardware) and now running live on the Mac target. Bundle writer, controller lifecycle, reducer, static-HTML report generator, and CLI verbs <code>run</code> / <code>validate-bundle</code> / <code>reduce</code> (post-hoc re-derivation of summary metrics from the recorded power trace and events) / <code>report</code>. Strict validation now also re-derives powermetrics traces from raw plist evidence, checks legacy additive-summary compatibility, and requires shape-valid provenance on new-era bundles. All bundle consumers read through one shared, tested read layer, which sharply reduces the risk of displayed numbers diverging from reported ones.</li> <li>Typed config and output schemas with validation, JSON-Schema export, and a CLI, plus the canonical suite run in CI on every push, including a mock end-to-end run and bundle validation. The command and CI output own the current result; reader docs do not copy its volatile count. Emitted configs round-trip their own published schema, and config hashes (run identity) are pinned by test.</li> <li>Adapter interface contracts (runtime / telemetry / transport), the run bundle artifact contract, and the measurement methodology (idle subtraction, measurement boundaries, clock synchronization, statistical protocol - highlights below).</li> <li>Evidence-shaped plans for every phase, a design-decision log whose index is mechanically checked against its decision bodies (with D-060 ratified by Ed); the log itself is the structural authority, and most entries record the alternatives considered), a risk register with an explicit descope ladder, and example configs for the Mac and mock targets.</li> <li>The complete Mac vertical slice: the MLX runtime adapter (2G), the <code>powermetrics</code> telemetry adapter (2H, parser pinned to a captured privileged sample, raw plists preserved verbatim in every bundle), and the flagship integration (2I) — three strict-valid repetition bundles of real energy measurements on the M3 Max. <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per 512-token request. <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~44.4 J per request and ~79-90 mJ per generated output token. TTFT was ~94 ms at 257 tokens/s; these are legacy L1 preliminary observations for provisional model Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit, mirrored locally. The separately recorded <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request; <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. These historical values are basis labels on the recorded results, not a new reduction.</li> <li>The P2-042 frozen analysis manifest, P2-041 campaign verdict split, P2-037 contrast/claim engine, P2-040 reducer/gate remainder, P2-038 production-uncertainty software path, and NV-GATE-2 code-now hardening. Reducer dispatch is frozen across the legacy and 0.3.x arms and current through 0.4.2. None of this promotes fixture-first NVIDIA evidence to live validation.</li> <li>The report&#39;s related-work survey draft (11 sources with verified citations and an honest positioning audit) and an off-machine iCloud Drive backup whose fresh restored bundles passed strict validation and were byte-identical to their sources.</li> </ul> <p>Live remote-hardware validation has not started: NVIDIA/vLLM and Jetson Orin promotion (2K/2L) remain gated on device access. The fixture-first implementation and NV-GATE-2 software hardening are landed, but all remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until live hardware contact; a P1-006 evidence checklist exists there. Code-level specs are in <code>docs/phase_2/hardware_slice_implementation_guide.md</code>. The mock-first core landed first by design, so measurement code is never debugging the measurement harness and a live hardware integration at the same time.</p> <p>Waiting on external input (most of it does not block current software work; P0-003&#39;s backup gate is satisfied, and the grading rubric/calendar (P1-008) carries the provisional-contract fallback under ratified D-060):</p> <ol> <li>NVIDIA / Jetson Orin device access evidence — the one hard gate left, for the remote-target slices 2K/2L. (The <code>nvidia_3050</code> in the architecture table is the owned always-available NVIDIA target; the 3080 Ti is a separate, borrowed card used only for Phase 3&#39;s interconnect sweep.)</li> <li>Calendar anchors: colloquium date, report deadline, and the 3080 Ti borrow window, to derive phase target dates.</li> <li>Advisor scope confirmation (see the sanity-check note above) — finalizes model selection; deliberately deprioritized while all work remains harness-shaped and valuable under any scope.</li> </ol> <p>Closed since the last revision: the comprehensive audit; AXI-SA&#39;s burst-decode contract; SITE-02 D1/D2; the SPLIT-AP Part I pre-registration freeze; AXI-SB&#39;s <code>supported</code> static-batch verdict with its Mac C5-2.2 leg; P2-038&#39;s production-shaped live gate; and AXI-SC&#39;s <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> pinned- runtime verdict. The later DSpark/DFlash MLX feasibility smokes and D-075 extension-axis intake are recorded without promoting an energy claim, and the nine-bundle OLMoE/Qwen follow-on remains explicitly exploratory. Window A&#39;s software gates are satisfied, its first floor corpus is published, and the window remains open. The floors are calibration thresholds rather than claim promotion: P2-037 adjudication remains pending because strict-valid collection and claim readiness are separate gates; execution timing is governed by the live work-selection state in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>&#39;s generated state-kernel region and still requires Ed plus a quiet Mac.</p> <h2 id="architecture">Architecture</h2> <pre><code class="language-text">typed config

review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. docs/strategy/2026-08-06-impressiveness-roadmap.md:166:For the wall-meter path, the right class is a calibrated bench AC power analyzer, not an inexpensive consumer plug. A concrete baseline is the Yokogawa WT310E: its manufacturer lists 10 readings/s, USB export, 0.1%-of-reading plus 0.05%-of-range basic accuracy, high crest-factor capability, and a **$2,935 base US price** before calibration/fixture costs. Actual suitability still depends on calculating uncertainty at the Mac’s observed load and using a safe inline fixture. Borrowing an in-calibration unit from an engineering lab is preferable to spending several thousand dollars. [Yokogawa WT310E specifications and current price](https://tmi.yokogawa.com/us/solutions/products/power-analyzers/digital-power-meter-wt300e/).
docs/strategy/2026-08-06-impressiveness-roadmap.md:175:| **ICPE full research track** | Plausible over months, but not yet supported by the current evidence. ICPE 2027 lists research and artifact tracks but their details and dates remain TBA. The 2026 research track used 10 pages and judged novelty, technical quality, and scientific soundness; 2026’s reported full-paper acceptance rate was 28%. [ICPE 2027](https://icpe2027.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [2026 research criteria](https://icpe2026.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [acceptance history](https://icpe.spec.org/past-conferences/) | C1–C8, cross-day stability, artifact-ready release, and at least one deeper contribution: held-out Q4 prediction, second-unit replication, or a successful mechanism study. Split is not required. |

low / medium / high, judged against the current phase.</li> <li>Trigger: the observable event that means the risk is materializing.</li> <li>Mitigation: what we do <em>now</em> to reduce likelihood or impact.</li> <li>Fallback: what we do <em>if it happens</em> - every fallback must preserve a publishable result, even if smaller.</li> <li>Owner: <code>user</code> for actions needing Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (wrong deliverable built).</li> <li>Trigger: Phase 2 implementation slices ready to start (2A-2F complete) with P1-001 still open; or any supervisor communication contradicting <code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code> scope.</li> <li>Status note (2026-07-05): the first trigger fired 2026-06-12 (2A-2F completed with P1-001 still open). The mitigation is holding as designed - all work since has been hardware-independent and harness-shaped (mock slice, docs, Slice 2N is next and is also ungated) - and the fallback (&quot;continue only mock/local work; hardware purchases/borrows blocked-on-approval&quot;) is effectively in force.</li> <li>Mitigation: the queue keeps P1-001 ranked first; all work until approval stays hardware-independent and harness-shaped (valuable under any scope); the Phase 1 exit checklist lists the exact questions to put to the supervisor so one meeting can close the gate.</li> <li>Fallback: if approval stalls past mock-slice completion, continue only mock/local work and mark every hardware purchase or borrow decision blocked-on-approval.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-002-powermetrics-sudo-workflow-not-approved-on-measurement-mac">R-002: powermetrics sudo workflow not approved on measurement Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low (user controls the machine; a local auth session needs rescheduling - the planned 2026-06-10 slot passed without one). Impact: high (no Mac telemetry = no flagship vertical slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with privileged powermetrics capture and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new macOS/MLX/powermetrics versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: scoped sudoers rule (D-004) cannot be installed, or privileged sample capture fails after the auth session.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-004 defines a minimal, single-binary sudoers rule with the exact line documented in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s instrumentation section; interactive-sudo manual fallback documented for attended runs.</li> <li>Fallback: attended runs with interactive sudo (operator present per experiment); if even that is unacceptable, the Mac becomes runtime-supported/telemetry-blocked and the first real slice moves to the first available CUDA target - recorded as a finding, not hidden.</li> <li>Owner: user (install rule), agent (pre-check + structured failure).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-003-mlx-install-or-model-load-failure-on-mac">R-003: MLX install or model-load failure on Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (delays flagship slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with MLX generation and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new MLX/mlx-lm versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: <code>pip install mlx mlx-lm</code> fails, or the chosen model (D-016) has no working MLX artifact.</li> <li>Mitigation: install into a dedicated venv with versions recorded in run bundles; model criteria (D-016) require known MLX availability before selection; smoke-test load before scheduling measurement sessions.</li> <li>Fallback: llama.cpp with the Metal backend as the Mac runtime (already a planned runtime for split portability under D-015); the MLX adapter then becomes optional rather than flagship.</li> <li>Owner: agent (with user approving installs).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-004-kv-persist-resume-unsupported-in-a-target-runtime">R-004: KV persist/resume unsupported in a target runtime</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium overall (high for vLLM file-based replay, low for llama.cpp, low-medium for mlx-lm). Impact: high if unmitigated - this is the project&#39;s central feasibility risk.</li> <li>Trigger: a Stage 3.0 spike returns <code>replay_unsupported</code> for a runtime needed by a planned pairing.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-015&#39;s feasibility ladder - spikes run <em>before</em> any split hardware time is scheduled; pairings are planned only on runtimes with <code>replay_supported</code> verdicts; the synthetic transfer microbenchmark (Stage 3.1) is independent of all runtime cooperation and guarantees a crossover dataset.</li> <li>Fallback: analytical composition - measured prefill energy (node A) + measured synthetic transfer energy (payload sized by the KV model) + measured decode energy (node B) bounds the split cost honestly; the report states the composition method explicitly.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-005-llama-cpp-cache-files-not-portable-across-machines-backends">R-005: llama.cpp cache files not portable across machines/backends</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (session files are version- and model-sensitive; cross-backend CUDA-save -&gt; Metal-load is unverified). Impact: high for <em>heterogeneous</em> pairings specifically.</li> <li>Trigger: Stage 3.0.2&#39;s cross-machine restore test fails or produces divergent output.</li> <li>Mitigation: the spike tests cross-machine restore explicitly, with pinned identical llama.cpp versions and identical GGUF files on both ends, before any heterogeneous experiment is scheduled.</li> <li>Fallback: restrict offline-replay pairings to same-platform pairs (GPU-&gt;GPU in the borrow window, Orin-&gt;Orin); cover heterogeneous pairs with the analytical composition (R-004 fallback); report the portability finding itself - it is a legitimate disaggregation-practicality result.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-006-3080-ti-borrow-window-slips-or-shrinks">R-006: 3080 Ti borrow window slips or shrinks</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (loses GPU-&gt;GPU pairing, not the phase).</li> <li>Trigger: window not scheduled by Phase 3 Stage 3.2 completion; or window arrives before split tooling is ready.</li> <li>Mitigation: all split tooling reaches rehearsed-on-available-hardware state before the window (the Phase 3 plan keeps a borrow-window runbook so borrow time is execution-only, no debugging); calendar mapping task (P1-008) makes the window a tracked date.</li> <li>Fallback: GPU-&gt;GPU pairing drops to single-GPU prefill/decode phase decomposition plus analytical composition; 3050&lt;-&gt;Orin and Orin&lt;-&gt;Orin remain.</li> <li>Owner: user (scheduling), agent (runbook readiness).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-007-no-wall-meter-available">R-007: No wall meter available</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1-4. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (boundary calibration and Pi/Hailo coverage lost; per-target results stand).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-003 resolves &quot;unavailable&quot;.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-003 is a Phase 1 gate precisely so this resolves before it matters; D-018&#39;s boundary table makes results honest without a meter.</li> <li>Fallback: report within-target comparisons (always boundary-consistent) as primary; flag cross-target absolute comparisons with the boundary caveat; targets with no platform telemetry (Pi) become telemetry-unavailable findings.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-008-orin-telemetry-inaccessible">R-008: Orin telemetry inaccessible</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-3. Likelihood: medium (rail sysfs paths vary by L4T version). Impact: low (one target of several).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-006 evidence shows neither INA3221 sysfs nor tegrastats usable.</li> <li>Mitigation: two candidate mechanisms documented before hardware time; wall-meter fallback if R-007 resolves positively.</li> <li>Fallback: Orin runs runtime-only (latency/throughput) marked telemetry-unavailable, or drops to a stretch target.</li> <li>Owner: user (access), agent (adapter).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-009-hailo-cannot-run-llm-shaped-workloads">R-009: Hailo cannot run LLM-shaped workloads</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: high. Impact: low - <em>by design</em>: the plan treats Hailo as a feasibility investigation whose negative verdict is itself a reportable applicability finding.</li> <li>Status: <strong>realized as expected, 2026-06-12</strong> — verdict <code>unsupported_workload</code>. The trigger fired (a non-<code>supported</code> verdict), the by-design mitigation held, and the outcome is the publishable applicability finding the plan anticipated. No schedule impact.</li> <li>Trigger: feasibility checklist closes with any non-<code>supported</code> verdict. (Fired 2026-06-12.)</li> <li>Mitigation: none needed; the verdict-code structure in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s Hailo section makes the outcome publishable either way. Do not spend implementation effort on a Hailo backend (the verdict is now recorded; the standing do-not-do-yet rule becomes &quot;report, don&#39;t implement&quot;).</li> <li>Fallback: Pi 5 CPU-only llama.cpp with wall-meter telemetry becomes an optional low-power data point if the meter exists; otherwise Pi/Hailo appears only in the applicability table.</li> <li>Owner: user (device access), agent (verdict documentation - done).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-010-controller-as-dut-contamination-on-mac-runs">R-010: Controller-as-DUT contamination on Mac runs</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: high if unmitigated. Impact: medium (biased flagship numbers).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-013 (idle baseline includes resident quiescent controller; deferred logging; blocking wait during measured window).</li> <li>Trigger (residual): SSH-controlled comparison runs (once transport exists) show a delta beyond run-to-run variance.</li> <li>Fallback: move Mac headline measurements to remote-controlled runs.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-011-benchmark-network-cannot-be-isolated">R-011: Benchmark network cannot be isolated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (campus/home network constraints unknown until P1-004 closes). Impact: medium (noisy transfer measurements).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-004 topology answer shows shared links only.</li> <li>Mitigation: prefer direct node-to-node cabling (no switch) for 1GbE/2.5GbE point-to-point tests - removes the isolation question entirely for two-node experiments; record link conditions per run in the bundle.</li> <li>Fallback: run sweeps off-hours, repeat n&gt;=5, report observed throughput alongside nominal link speed (the bundle already records measured throughput per D-008&#39;s transfer block).</li> <li>Owner: user (hardware), agent (recording).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-012-schedule-five-phases-vs-fixed-academic-deadlines">R-012: Schedule: five phases vs fixed academic deadlines</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, not by code).</li> <li>Trigger: any phase exceeding its (to-be-set) calendar budget; colloquium or report dates announced (P1-008) leaving less runway than the plan assumes.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-008 maps phases to real dates as soon as the user supplies them (<code>docs/milestones.md</code> holds the skeleton); every phase defines a hardware-independent floor and a descope ladder so cutting is a decision, not a scramble.</li> <li>Descope ladder (worst-case minimum viable capstone, in cut order):<ol> <li>Drop live split (3.3) - already stretch.</li> <li>Drop 10GbE and one model size.</li> <li>Drop heterogeneous replay pairs (keep synthetic transfer + analytical composition).</li> <li>Drop Orin/Pi targets (keep Mac + one CUDA).</li> <li>Floor: mock harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + analytical split model. This is still a complete, defensible benchmark-plus-study.</li> </ol> </li> <li>Owner: user (dates), agent (floor discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-013-thermal-throttling-confounds-measurements">R-013: Thermal throttling confounds measurements</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-4. Likelihood: medium (high on passively-cooled Orin/Pi). Impact: medium (rep-to-rep drift, biased late reps).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-014 (idle-power recovery gate between reps, thermal_drift_c in measurement quality, interleaved ordering) - residual risk on targets without thermal sensors.</li> <li>Trigger: thermal_drift_c trending across reps, or cooldown cap hits recorded in bundles.</li> <li>Fallback: longer cooldowns, active cooling notes recorded in run metadata, or excluding throttled reps <em>with documented cause</em> per D-014.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-014-model-weights-become-unavailable-or-gated">R-014: Model weights become unavailable or gated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (mid-project model swap breaks comparability).</li> <li>Trigger: chosen model&#39;s hub entry gated/removed; license terms change.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-016 requires mirroring chosen weights to local storage immediately on selection, with revisions and hashes recorded.</li> <li>Fallback: promote the recorded fallback candidate; re-run affected baselines (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-015-schema-changes-after-data-collection-starts">R-015: Schema changes after data collection starts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (existing bundles unreadable or silently misread).</li> <li>Status: mitigated structurally.</li> <li>Mitigation: schema_version field exists from v0.1; D-008 plans the only anticipated breaking-shape change (v0.2) <em>before</em> split data collection; output-schema additions are additive-only (the JSON schema does not forbid additional properties); <code>validate-bundle</code> pins what a valid bundle means per version.</li> <li>Trigger: any proposed non-additive change to a schema with bundles already on disk.</li> <li>Fallback: a dated migration note in this repo plus a one-shot migration script; never edit bundles in place (they are evidence).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-016-measurement-corpus-loss-runs-has-no-backup-path">R-016: Measurement-corpus loss (runs/ has no backup path)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-5. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (the dataset behind every claim is a gitignored directory on one disk; a disk failure or an errant delete erases the evidence the defense rests on, and hardware re-collection needs access windows that may not recur).</li> <li>Trigger: first real (non-mock) bundle written; any data-affecting incident (disk error, iCloud eviction anomaly, accidental delete).</li> <li>Mitigation: before the first real measurement session (gate on 2I data collection, tracked as queue task P0-002), define and record the backup protocol here: destination (external disk and/or cloud location outside the repo), cadence (after every measurement session), method (rsync of <code>runs/</code> plus experiment manifests), and a restore test performed once. Configs + manifests already make re-collection well-defined; backups make it unnecessary.</li> <li><strong>Protocol recorded (2026-07-06, P0-002 closed interim).</strong> Destination: <code>~/JouleWise-backup</code> — a user-directed INTERIM location on the same disk (&quot;cursory... I&#39;ll handle that later&quot;); it protects against errant deletes but not disk failure, so the user still owes an external/cloud destination for full mitigation. Cadence: after every measurement session. Method: <code>scripts/backup_runs.sh [RUNS_DIR] [DEST]</code> (rsync -a, never <code>--delete</code>; dated UTC log line per invocation appended to <code>DEST/backup.log</code>). Restore test performed 2026-07-06: mock bundle backed up, restored to a temp dir, <code>validate-bundle</code> green on the restored copy. Swapping in the final destination is a one-argument change (or edit the script default) plus one fresh restore test.</li> <li><strong>Protocol upgraded (2026-07-10/11, P0-003 closed; addendum 2026-07-16 closing a summary-row/body drift found by the resumption audit).</strong> The interim same-disk destination above is superseded: the external destination is iCloud Drive, live with a fresh backup + restore test passed (evidence: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code> §11, &quot;The P0-003 iCloud measurement-corpus backup and restore gate is satisfied&quot;). The 2026-07-06 entry above is retained as history. Standing caveat: iCloud eviction — re-verify the destination is materialized (fresh restore test) before each measurement window.</li> <li>Fallback: re-run affected experiments from their configs (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly per D-005/D-010); report any unrecoverable gap honestly in the exclusion log.</li> <li>Owner: user (destination/media), agent (protocol doc + restore test).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-017-repo-lives-on-icloud-synced-desktop-eperm-lock-recurrence">R-017: Repo lives on iCloud-synced Desktop (EPERM lock recurrence)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: low (mitigated; was high while on Desktop). Impact: medium (blocks work sessions mid-run; small integrity risk around eviction during writes).</li> <li>Status: <strong>mitigated 2026-07-05</strong> - the repo moved off the synced Desktop (current canonical path: <code>~/code/JouleWise</code>; the interim <code>~/code/CapstoneRivoire/Capstone</code> path recorded here was itself later renamed - corrected 2026-07-09, C-027). P0-001 complete; git + suite verified green at the new path. Residual exposure: agent sessions launched from the stale Desktop path (delete the leftover <code>~/Desktop/CapstoneRivoire</code> husk after relaunching from the new path), and any future placement of repo or <code>runs/</code> data under an iCloud-synced directory - do not.</li> <li>Trigger: any <code>Operation not permitted</code> on read/readdir inside the repo with the iCloud file provider (<code>bird</code>) active.</li> <li>History: first incident 2026-06-12 (documented in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>); recurred 2026-07-05 mid-run - <code>docs/</code>, <code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code>, <code>.git</code>, and the repo root EPERM-locked intermittently during an active iCloud full-sync, clearing and re-locking per subtree. Both incidents match iCloud &quot;Optimize Mac Storage&quot; behavior on <code>~/Desktop/</code>. The move landed the same day as the second incident.</li> <li>Fallback: if a lock ever strikes again, wait for it to clear (both incidents did), then re-verify with the test suite before continuing; the remote (<code>origin/main</code>) bounds code loss to the working tree.</li> <li>Owner: user (launch paths), agent (post-lock verification discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-018-the-agent-loop-itself-as-a-schedule-and-scope-risk">R-018: The agent loop itself as a schedule and scope risk</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, R-012).</li> <li>Registered by C-027 (NEGSPACE lens finding accepted in council): the multi-agent workflow can remain locally productive - packs, registries, meta-process, site work - while the graded deliverable path (rubric, report source, backup, real corpus, figures) stays starved. Same-day evidence at registration: ~6M tokens of breadth work vs six real corpus bundles, no report source, same-disk backup.</li> <li>Trigger: an agent-heavy work block that produces neither a new real evidence bundle nor a report/figure increment.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-060 depth-before-breadth stop line (RATIFIED by Ed 2026-07-10) extended by the WO-022/R2 spend guardrails (<code>docs/orchestration.md</code> §Spend guardrails, 2026-07-15); RPT-001 vertical slice; the C-027 correctness rows ranked ahead of all breadth work.</li> <li>Owner: lead (queue discipline + guardrail checkpoints), Ed (HARD bands and structure).</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/risk_register.md · commit dbd8137 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:29:The largest benchmark-quality gap is accuracy. The three telemetry boundaries use vendor-reported telemetry with uncharacterized absolute error -- one modeled, two sensor-backed but uncalibrated -- and no independent cross-check exists. The confirmed Jetson leg brings the program's first physical shunt measurement, with INA3221 datasheet bounds rather than a pure vendor model. The claims architecture handles this honestly -- no published claim routes through sensor trueness, within-boundary relative comparisons are the primary claim type, and monotone sensor distortion leaves ordinal claims intact -- so the missing calibration caps the claim ceiling rather than invalidating claims made. But the cap is real: absolute joules, cross-boundary winners, and cross-lab comparability are all out of reach, and condition-dependent telemetry bias could in principle contaminate even permitted relative claims undetectably. This is the one thing MLPerf Power's calibrated-analyzer regime delivers that JouleWise's entire rigor stack cannot substitute for -- while MLPerf, conversely, has no instrument at all for the per-rail, per-device, split-stage quantities JouleWise measures. One repo defect follows directly: the related-work draft claims rails are "calibrated against a wall meter where one exists" while the risk register records that none exists; this should be corrected.
docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:44:8. **Carbon-accounting and procurement readers** -- deferred with named gates (wall meter, second unit, cross-lab replication), not excluded by construction; the kill list correctly bars carbon labels and battery estimates today.
docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:55:4. **Q6 -- rails-vs-wall boundary bias.** Moderate standalone novelty (RAPL-vs-wall studies exist for CPUs) but the most load-bearing gated question: it is load-bearing for the entire software-counter literature and produces the named calibration bundle that any quantitative cross-boundary split claim requires.
docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:62:1. **The edifice validates internal consistency, never sensor truth.** Every joule in the current corpus is an unaudited vendor model; strict validation is structurally incapable of detecting systematic rail-model bias. *Defusal:* a wall-meter calibration bundle at a few steady load points (bounding the composite rails-vs-wall gap; the planned Jetson leg is already a physical shunt measurement).
docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:64:3. **The discrete-GPU transfer-energy hole.** On nvidia-smi ends, TCP byte movement is host CPU/NIC/DRAM work the board-power boundary excludes entirely, so measured "transfer energy" there is near-zero net -- a silent undercount in unmeasured silicon, asymmetric across the pairing matrix. *Defusal:* wall-meter the GPU host for transfer legs, or explicitly scope those cells as board-only lower bounds in the stage accounting before collection.
docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:73:JouleWise is an instrument-and-methodology contribution of genuine quality with one verified-unoccupied research target of real value. The audit chain, window discipline, and claim-gating stack together constitute the most rigorous measurement-integrity design in its class, and the program's two contamination catches -- one by human review before the gate existed, one by the gate's first true positive -- plus the formal self-demotion of its most quotable number show the discipline is operational, not performative. Against that: the sensors are unverified, the corpus is a demo, the claim gate has never fired beyond partial exercise on protocol, MDE arithmetic, and ladder classification, the flagship claim is currently forbidden in its strongest form by the project's own rules, and there is a concrete physical hole in the planned transfer-energy accounting on discrete-GPU ends. Published today it would be an excellent methods paper with a demonstration corpus. The distance to the strong version is short and fully enumerated by the project itself -- a wall meter, a seeded split analysis-plan row, a host-side boundary fix, floor calibration, and one campaign through the full chain -- after which the split corpus would be a first-of-kind dataset with an audit trail no peer can match. The program's merit is real; almost all of it is still ahead of the data.

docs/reviews/2026-07-09-scientific-rigor-review.md:236:   The docs are honest that wall meter calibration is missing and cross-boundary comparisons are descriptive. But an advisor would also ask for at least one external sanity check per backend to bound absolute telemetry trust. Failure scenario: powermetrics and nvidia-smi both pass strict validation, but both undercount memory/host energy, and the report’s “J/request” values are interpreted as system energy.

Require these caveats in report templates.
