## [orchestrator] Installed-API discovery before any design

Decision: Read the actual mlx_lm 0.31.3 cache API out of the venv
(`mlx_lm.models.cache`, `mlx_lm.generate.generate_step`, `mlx_lm.cache_prompt`)
rather than trusting the plan's remembered API surface.
Alternatives considered: trust the plan's `make/save/load_prompt_cache` memory and
the `mlx_lm.cache_prompt` CLI as-is.
Why: D-015 / the spike brief explicitly warn mlx_lm APIs move; the plan's own
3.0.1 text says "verify against the installed version, do not trust this plan's
memory of the API". Confirmed surface: `make_prompt_cache(model, max_kv_size)`,
`save_prompt_cache(file, cache, metadata)`, `load_prompt_cache(file,
return_metadata)`, `trim_prompt_cache(cache, n)`, `can_trim_prompt_cache(cache)`;
`generate_step(prompt, model, *, max_tokens, prompt_cache, ...)` with a default
greedy (argmax) sampler.
Confidence: High — read from source in the exact venv the live runs use. Would
change if a different venv/mlx_lm version were used for the live run.
Binds: the spike script and all resume logic in this stream.

## [orchestrator] Fresh-process resume isolation via subprocess-per-stage

Decision: The deliverable proves cross-process replay by running monolithic,
prefill, and decode as three SEPARATE OS processes (subprocess with
`sys.executable`), passing state only through files on disk (the cache
safetensors + a `prompt_tokens.json`), never through shared Python objects.
Alternatives considered: (a) single-process demo that just re-instantiates the
model — rejected: cannot rule out lingering module/global/mx state and does not
model the real A->B node split; (b) two top-level scripts — rejected: more files,
same guarantee, worse cohesion than subcommands in one script.
Why: the spike question is specifically "resume in a FRESH process". Separate
interpreters make in-memory reuse structurally impossible; the decode process
reads the prompt token ids the prefill process persisted (it does NOT
re-tokenize), so tokenizer drift cannot confound the identity comparison either.
Confidence: High. What would change my mind: if a reviewer shows a shared-state
channel that survives process boundaries and could alter the token stream (OS
page cache / mlx on-disk cache affect only timings, not correctness).
Binds: the isolation architecture reviewers audit at the diff gate.

## [orchestrator] Resume boundary = save at full offset, trim-by-1, feed last token

Decision: Prefill with `generate_step(prompt, max_tokens=0)` (cache ends at
offset == len(prompt)); on resume, `trim_prompt_cache(cache, 1)` back to
len(prompt)-1 and feed only `prompt[-1:]` into a 64-token greedy decode.
Alternatives considered: (a) prefill `prompt[:-1]` so the saved cache already
sits at len-1 — rejected: less faithful to the canonical `mlx_lm.cache_prompt`
flow (which saves the full prompt) and pushes the off-by-one into the writer
instead of making it explicit at resume; (b) feed `prompt[-1:]` WITHOUT trimming
— WRONG: the last token is already in the saved cache, so this double-counts it
and corrupts the logits.
Why: `generate_step` prefills `prompt[:-1]` in bulk then runs a step on the last
token that ALSO advances the cache — so a `max_tokens=0` prefill leaves the FULL
prompt in the cache. Reproducing the monolithic decode boundary therefore
requires rewinding exactly one token. Verified live in-process: all 64 resumed
tokens byte-identical to the monolithic run.
Confidence: High — empirically confirmed (IDENTICAL: True). Would change if a
future mlx_lm alters the prefill/step boundary; the script asserts offsets so a
regression surfaces loudly.
Binds: the correctness claim of the whole spike.

## [orchestrator] Prompt length 1024, decode 64

Decision: Feasibility runs use a 1024-token prompt and 64 greedy decode tokens.
Alternatives considered: the plan's 512/2048/8192 sweep and 256-token decode.
Why: 3.0.1 is a feasibility spike, not a benchmark (brief: keep prompts 512-2048,
decode <=64). 1024 is a clean mid-point that gives a non-trivial cache (~28 MiB)
for a meaningful size-vs-prediction check while keeping load light; the kv-size
predictor is exercised at the same 1024 length. The full length sweep belongs to
Stage 3.4, not the feasibility verdict. The script parameterizes prompt-len so a
larger length can be re-run without code change.
Confidence: High for the feasibility purpose.
Binds: the numbers recorded in kv_feasibility.md for 3.0.1.

## [orchestrator] Verdict code derived from measured data, not hardcoded

Decision: The script computes the verdict from measured outcomes (token identity
+ cache-size tolerance) rather than asserting `replay_supported`; a regression
flips it to `partial(...)`/`replay_unsupported` with the failing reason.
Alternatives considered: hardcode the expected `replay_supported`.
Why: D-015 makes negative verdicts first-class deliverables; an honest spike must
be able to report failure. The provisional live evidence points to
`replay_supported` (identity holds, size within 0.02% of prediction), but the
recorded verdict must come from the run, not the author.
Confidence: High on the principle; the final verdict code is set from the live
fresh-process run, not this in-process probe.
Binds: the verdict recorded for 3.0.1 and the exit-checklist row.

### C-6 [codex, transcribed by orchestrator] [type: code-shape] Decode stage trusts persisted prompt ids; model path cross-checked, not re-derived

Decision: The `decode` subcommand takes the model path from
`prompt_tokens.json` (written by the prefill process) and treats a passed
`--model` only as an assertion against it; prompt ids are never re-tokenized in
the decode process. Cache-size prediction imports `joulewise.kv_size` helpers
directly instead of parsing the CLI's stdout.
Alternatives: re-tokenize in decode (rejected: tokenizer drift could confound
the identity claim); parse `kv-size` CLI output (rejected by Codex after
reading `joulewise/kv_size.py`: clean importable functions exist).
Why: keeps the token-identity comparison grounded solely in artifacts crossing
the process boundary; import beats stdout-parsing for robustness.
Evidence: `scripts/spike_mlx_prompt_cache.py` (`cmd_decode`,
`predict_cache_bytes`); Codex final messages
`docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/codex-impl-round1.md` and
`.../codex-impl-round2.md`, incl. Codex's isolation judgment: subprocess-per-stage is airtight
against in-process reuse; residual paths (OS page cache, mmap, compiled-kernel
caches) affect timings only, not correctness.
Confidence: High.
Binds: how 3.0.1 evidence is generated; template for 3.0.2's script shape.
Depends-on: C-2 (subprocess isolation), C-3 (trim-by-1 boundary).

### C-7 [orchestrator] [type: acceptance] 3.0.1 verdict evidence = two lengths (1024, 2048), fresh-process, greedy 64

Decision: The recorded `replay_supported` verdict rests on two live
fresh-process runs (prompt 1024 and 2048, decode 64 greedy), both
token-identical with cache sizes +0.018% / +0.009% over the kv-size
prediction (~5.3 KiB constant safetensors header). The size model is declared
usable for sweep planning with a "+~5 KiB fixed" correction, no multiplicative
calibration.
Alternatives: single length (weaker scaling evidence); full 512/2048/8192
sweep (rejected: benchmarking, belongs to Stage 3.4).
Why: two lengths distinguish a constant header from a proportional error at
negligible extra cost; D-015 wants a feasibility verdict, not a dataset.
Evidence: `docs/phase_3/kv_feasibility.md` §3.0.1 (results table);
`docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/spike_report_{1024,2048}.json`;
headline command
`.venv/bin/python3 scripts/spike_mlx_prompt_cache.py run --prompt-len 1024 --decode 64`.
Confidence: High for feasibility; timings are explicitly non-benchmark.
Binds: the 3.0.1 row in the exit checklist and 3.0.4 consolidation.

### C-8 [orchestrator, transcribing 2 lenses] [type: process] Two should-fix hardening findings — accepted, deferred, non-blocking to the verdict

Decision: Both counterreview lenses cleared the `replay_supported` verdict and
each raised exactly one `should-fix` (no blockers). Both are accepted as valid
and DEFERRED (a designed fix exists and was reverted under the session stop
order to keep the committed script coherent with the live-generated report
artifacts); neither weakens the recorded verdict.
Findings:
1. Isolation lens — `run_stage()` prepends repo root but preserves an inherited
   `PYTHONPATH`; a shadowing `mlx_lm` on the path could be imported while
   `importlib.metadata.version` still reports 0.31.3, faking the "installed
   mlx-lm" provenance. Not triggered by the recorded runs (clean repo-venv env,
   no PYTHONPATH shadow). Fix (designed): record each subprocess's resolved
   `mlx_lm.__file__` in the report and require the three stages agree.
2. Evidence lens — `verdict_for` could emit `replay_supported` on two equal
   short/empty token lists; the JSON records requested `decode_tokens: 64`, not
   observed generated counts, so the "64/64" doc claim leans on runtime
   behaviour. Not triggered (both recorded runs generated exactly 64). Fix
   (designed): derive observed counts from the recorded token lists and gate the
   verdict on `mono==resume==requested`.
Why defer not fix now: findings are robustness/evidence-provenance, not
correctness of THIS run; the stop order directed finalize-not-fix; landing the
fix cleanly requires regenerating the committed report JSONs, out of scope for
the checkpoint. Recommend folding both into the 3.0.2 shared spike-script shape
(the llama.cpp spike will reuse this harness).
Evidence: `docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/lens-isolation.md`;
`docs/stream_logs/2026-07-07-kv-spike-301/lens-evidence.md`.
Confidence: High that neither blocks the 3.0.1 verdict; both fixes are cheap.
Binds: the 3.0.2 script-hardening backlog; does not alter the 3.0.1 verdict.
Depends-on: C-2, C-7.

### C-CHECKPOINT [orchestrator] [type: acceptance] Stream checkpoint — 3.0.1 verdict final

Verdict: **`replay_supported`** (Stage 3.0.1, mlx-lm 0.31.3, Mac/Metal) — FINAL
for the feasibility question. No pending work blocks it; the two C-8 findings

hardware and calibration manifest are known.

| claim_role | primary |

Excluded long profiles require named `DROP-FEASIBILITY-P1-004-P1-006-BOUNDARY-PROFILE` evidence before any campaign bundle exists. |
| multiplicity_rule | Holm within FAM-Q6-RAIL-WALL-BOUNDARY across predeclared workload-profile boundary deltas and conclusion-flip tests. Any post-hoc workload, boundary, or backend subset is exploratory. |
| Metric + exact window class | Primary: workload-induced delta energy by boundary on gross request windows and idle-subtracted request windows: `delta_external_j`, `delta_platform_j`, `external_minus_platform_j`, and sign/direction of any conclusion flip. Calibration descriptors may include session-window idle and sustained blocks. |
| Unit of analysis + dependence structure | Paired block: the same workload execution or matched active block with simultaneous platform telemetry and external meter trace. Platform and external readings in a block are dependent paired measurements. |
| Estimator/formula | Fit or summarize paired boundary difference `external_minus_platform_j = delta_external_j - delta_platform_j` by workload family. If at least three active load levels exist, fit the detection-floor runbook bridge `delta_external_j = alpha + beta * delta_platform_j + residual_j`; quantitative bridge accepted only when held-out or cross-validated residuals satisfy the P2-015 threshold. A conclusion-flip test is predeclared as whether a same-condition ordering changes sign between boundary estimates. |
| Inclusion/exclusion + quality-flag waiver rules | Strict-valid JouleWise bundles plus external meter artifact required. Exclude blocks without synchronization evidence, meter calibration/status, meter cadence, platform rail manifest, shared marker plan/manual sync note, or matched window definitions. Waivers must be named in the frozen registry and cannot turn missing external evidence into a calibrated claim. |

For repeated LLM workloads, counterbalance profile order per D-014/C-011 conventions and record cooldown cap hits. Include block/session and meter-cadence covariates only if frozen. |

Canonical `mid_mid` is 1024/256. Any 8192/256 long-prompt request cell and any 2048/2048 request cell are capped until P2-015 adds matching-or-harder cells or the frozen AP names an accepted AP-specific bound; ambiguous coverage must consume every plausible harder cell and take the maximum floor. The JouleWise workload half is current v0.1. External-meter capture/import is
PLANNED under P1-003 wall-meter evidence and P2-015 calibration runbooks. The

Order policy: execute repeated profiles in ABBA-like paired order where A and B
are identical JouleWise workload labels under simultaneous external metering.
For step-load calibration, alternate idle and sustained active blocks with at
least three transitions and reverse the active-load order across blocks.

For `workload_profile.repetitions > 1`, the current runner dispatches to the
experiment runner: member bundles are written as `runs/<base_run_id>__r1` ...
`runs/<base_run_id>__rN`, and the manifest lands at
`runs/experiments/<base_run_id>.json`. Validation, reduction, import, and
packaging paths must name member bundles, not the base `run_id`.

## Expected Artifacts

Standard run bundles must contain `config.json`, `metadata.json`,
`events.jsonl`, `power_trace.csv`, raw telemetry under `raw/`, logs, outputs,
and `summary_metrics.json`, per `docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md`.

Additional expected external-meter artifacts:

```text
runs/<base_run_id>__rN/
  external_meter/
    meter_metadata.json
    trace.csv
    sync_notes.json
```

`metadata.json` must include the platform rail manifest required by D-018.
`external_meter/meter_metadata.json` records make/model, calibration
date/status, stated accuracy, resolution, sampling cadence, logging mode, and
synchronization method. The marker/clock-offset expectations follow D-003:
shared marker plan or manual synchronization notes are recorded, and any
window shorter than the recorded clock/sync bound is not used for attribution.

Comparisons are like-window and like-workload only: platform request window
against external request window, platform idle block against external idle
block. Cross-boundary ranking language is not allowed unless the paired bridge
clears its predeclared residual threshold.

## Figure Skeletons

F-Q6-BOUNDARY-SCATTER: external vs platform workload-induced energy.

- x-axis: platform rail/model energy delta (J), boundary label
  `<<RAIL_BACKEND>>`.
- y-axis: external meter energy delta (J), boundary label `wall_meter full
  system AC` or `USB-C PD/DC input`.
- Caption template: `Measurements in this figure characterize one physical unit of [target hardware] running [OS/version], [runtime/library], [model artifact], [quantization], [tokenizer], [sampler/output policy], and [measurement boundary]. They support stack-specific claims under the stated boundary and do not establish hardware-class, vendor-class, or unit-general results without independent replication or calibration evidence.`

F-Q6-BOUNDARY-RESIDUALS: bridge residual by workload family.

- x-axis: workload family/block.
- y-axis: `external_minus_platform_j` residual (J).
- Caption adds: `Boundary labels differ across cells, so absolute energy values are descriptive rather than a calibrated cross-target ranking.` when residual threshold has not cleared.

F-Q6-CONCLUSION-FLIP: direction by boundary.

- x-axis: frozen workload contrast.
- y-axis: paired contrast energy (J), with separate rail and wall/PD points.
- Caption states whether the flip test was predeclared and whether it cleared
  the floor gate.

## Hardware Prerequisites

- P1-003 wall meter or PD/DC analyzer decision, including export/logging
  method.
- P2-015 calibration artifact with the exact request-window floor rows named
  in the AP row.
- Platform telemetry backend and rail manifest for `<<TARGET_DEVICE>>`.
- Synchronization method that satisfies D-003 and P2-015 clock-bound gates.

## Plug-In-Day Runbook

Existing commands:

```sh
python3 -m joulewise validate-config configs/campaign_packs/<<Q6_CONFIG>>.json
python3 -m joulewise run configs/campaign_packs/<<Q6_CONFIG>>.json --runs-dir runs
python3 scripts/run_campaign.py configs/campaign_packs/<<Q6_CONFIG_DIR>> --runs-dir runs --log runs/experiments/<<Q6_EXPERIMENT_ID>>.jsonl --backup
python3 -m joulewise validate-bundle --strict runs/<<BASE_RUN_ID>>__r1
python3 -m joulewise reduce runs/<<BASE_RUN_ID>>__r1
python3 scripts/package_bundle_pack.py --output runs/bundle_packs/<<PACK_ID>> runs/<<BASE_RUN_ID_A>>__r1 runs/<<BASE_RUN_ID_B>>__r1
python3 scripts/package_bundle_pack.py --verify runs/bundle_packs/<<PACK_ID>>
```

PLANNED commands:

```sh
# PLANNED, owner: P1-003 wall-meter evidence plus P2-015 calibration runbook.
python3 -m joulewise import-external-meter --bundle runs/<<BASE_RUN_ID>>__r1 --trace <<METER_TRACE_CSV>> --metadata <<METER_METADATA_JSON>>

# PLANNED, owner: P2-015 floor/calibration implementation.
python3 -m joulewise boundary-calibrate runs/<<BASE_RUN_ID_A>>__r1 runs/<<BASE_RUN_ID_B>>__r1 --output runs/analysis/<<Q6_RESULTS>>.json
```

Operator sequence:

0. Acquire the no-agent quiet-machine lock (`[QUIET-MAC]`; see
   `docs/orchestration.md`): stop all agent/Codex load for the whole
   measurement session and confirm machine-idle state before the first idle
   baseline.
1. Create `configs/campaign_packs/` if needed, copy the filled template JSON
   into that directory, record meter make/model/calibration/export method, and
   freeze the AP row with complete contrast IDs.
2. Resolve all selection-scope alternatives to included/excluded verdicts
   before any campaign bundle exists, using named evidence such as
   `DROP-FEASIBILITY-P1-004-P1-006-BOUNDARY-PROFILE` for excluded profiles.
3. Generate or hand-author `configs/campaign_packs/<<Q6_CONFIG_DIR>>/order_manifest.json`
   with schema `joulewise.order_manifest.v1`, including paired ABBA-like
   profile order and start/end `short_short_sentinel` entries that must execute
   as the first and last measured bundles bracketing each hardware session.
   See `docs/campaign_packs/README.md` for the campaign-order versus
   intra-suite-order distinction. Extending `scripts/generate_matrix.py` for Q6
   boundary matrices is a PLANNED prerequisite owned by Phase 3 Stage 3.1 if
   the manifest is not hand-authored.
4. Start external meter logging, run JouleWise workload bundles, and preserve
   meter traces with synchronization notes.
5. Strict-validate and reduce JouleWise member bundles
   (`runs/<base_run_id>__rN`) and retain `runs/experiments/<base_run_id>.json`.
6. Import/pair external traces once the planned importer exists; otherwise
   keep external artifacts adjacent to bundles and cap claims at L1/descriptive.

Closing cooldown-gate note: the D-014 cooldown gate between repetitions is
runner-automated, but cooldown cap-hit flags must be checked in each member
bundle's measurement quality before analysis.

Global label: every quantitative value below is **NON-CLAIM / DIAGNOSTIC**.

## Desk recommendation

**VERDICT: MARGINAL.**

At the historically measured workload—Qwen2.5 1.5B versus 7B, identical 128-token prompt and 512-token fixed output—the best ABBA estimate is a 7B−1.5B prefill delta of **5.809930 J**. The decision-log practical bar is only approximately **5 J**, leaving **0.809930 J**, or about **16%**, of point-estimate headroom.

That is not enough to recommend adding the contrast at its existing 128-token shape. The default fork should therefore be:

- claim prefill floors;
- retain the model contrast as decode-only;
- describe the 128-token prefill contrast as infeasible-to-clear-with-comfort in limitations.

A prospectively frozen 256-token prompt could change the answer: proportional sensitivity gives approximately **11.619860 J**, comfortably above the approximate bar. Because no historical 7B corpus above 128 prompt tokens exists, that is a sizing projection, not demonstrated evidence.

## Verified doctrine and conflict check

[D-078 clause 11](</Users/edr/code/JouleWise/docs/decision_log.md:4599>) says:

- attribution error is roughly **0.7–1.0 J** per phase member;
- the instrument is attribution-limited rather than noise-limited;
- the practical effective clearable effect is **floor + claim-side bound, approximately 5 J for phase contrasts**;
- workload length is the free lever because the attribution error is approximately duration-independent while the effect scales with workload.

There is no exact **5.000000 J** threshold in the decision log. It is explicitly approximate.

[D-083](</Users/edr/code/JouleWise/docs/decision_log.md:5130>) adds an important wording correction: the expression is not a single summed acceptance gate. The floor gate and claim decision interval are enforced separately; approximately **5 J** remains the correct practical description of what an effect must jointly clear. Thus, if “effective claim bar” in the prompt meant one literal acceptance threshold, the decision log narrows that wording.

D-110 does not void the PASSED windows themselves, but it makes the old minted floors non-claim-bearing because their never-zero allowance was understated. Consequently, old point energies remain usable here as diagnostics; old floor or interval values cannot be promoted.

## Contrast uncertainty composition

For a 7B−1.5B contrast, energy points subtract but uncertainty magnitudes add. D-078’s contrast rule is `Σ|cᵢ|wᵢ`, not root-sum-square.

In the direct ABBA corpus:

- mean 1.5B prefill anchor half-width: **0.768096 J**;
- mean 7B prefill anchor half-width: **1.039955 J**;
- ABBA block-composed contrast half-width: mean **1.808052 J**, range **1.713501–1.908734 J**.

Applying that historical composed half-width to the point delta gives a diagnostic interval of approximately **4.001878–7.617982 J**. Its lower side falls below the practical approximately **5 J** bar. Moreover, D-110 shows that the old minted uncertainty was understated, so these historical widths must not be used to argue for a lower bar.

D-082’s “max, never sum” rule concerns absolute versus comparative components inside one floor cell. It does not authorize RSS or non-composition of the two model measurements in a model contrast.

## Length sensitivity

A purely proportional diagnostic inversion gives nominal break-even at approximately **110 prompt tokens**, which explains why the observed 128-token point estimate is only barely over the practical bar.

Projected from the matched 128-token ABBA delta:

| Prompt length | Projected delta | Point ratio to approximate bar | Interpretation |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 128 tokens | 5.809930 J observed | 1.16× | Marginal |
| 192 tokens | 8.714895 J projected | 1.74× | Likely clear, but still extrapolated |
| 256 tokens | 11.619860 J projected | 2.32× | Recommended sizing if the contrast is retained |

The 1.5B clean corpus supports approximate scaling: multiplying its 128-token mean by **32** predicts **52.770445 J**, versus **51.072749 J** observed at 4096 tokens, an approximately **3.3%** difference. That is encouraging, but it is not a substitute for missing long-prompt 7B evidence.

## Rough ABBA arm and runtime

For a retained, lengthened contrast:

- fixed A/B/B/A order;
- ten blocks;
- forty cross-model members total;
- same prompt-token hash across models;
- prospective prompt length of at least 256 tokens;
- `phase_energy_j.prefill` explicitly registered before collection.

The proven 128-token contrast’s forty members took approximately **106.7 minutes** from the first member completion to the last. Window B’s forty-member prefill ABBA took approximately **109.4 minutes**. Thus budget roughly **110 minutes** core, or about **130 minutes** with a 20% member-failure margin.

The proven ten-absolute companion took roughly **25–28 minutes**. A ten-absolute plus forty-null floor design is therefore about **135 minutes** of science-member time before calibrations and references.

Adding a separate forty-member cross-model contrast produces about **245 minutes** of core science-member time before references, calibration, adjudication, and failure margin. That likely exceeds the project’s two-to-four-hour preferred window envelope. If the parent retains the contrast, splitting floor and contrast collection into separate quiet windows is safer than compressing both.

## Scheduling matrix

| Row | action | wait_for | collision surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing 128-token contrast | do_not_start | None | Too little margin over the approximate bar |
| Prospectively sized 256-token contrast | needs_ruling | Workload-size/preregistration ruling and current claim-window readiness gates | Adds about 110 core minutes; likely collides with the floor window’s runtime envelope |

## 1. JouleWise-Q4: Predicting Request Energy from Prompt and Output Shape

**Thesis.** After calibrating what differences are resolvable, a simple fixed-plus-prefill-plus-decode model can either predict held-out LLM workloads on the named M3 Max stack or expose reproducible interactions that invalidate that abstraction.

**Project brief and steps.** JouleWise already has the scientific spine: calibrated phase attribution, attribution-limited floors, two independent claim gates, and fail-closed custody. The immediate work remains the D-117 desk machinery followed by three prospective windows: 1.5B and 7B decode floors with prefill riders, then the decode contrast. Those results become this paper’s calibrated anchors rather than merely demonstrations. Next, freeze AP-1’s `4×3` grid—prompt `{128,512,2048,4096}` × output `{64,256,512}`—with `(512,256)` and `(4096,512)` held out. Collect one magnitude/null-ladder window and one grid window per model: **three additional quiet windows**, each independently bracketed and custodied. Then mint matching floors, fit only the training cells, evaluate held-outs once, and populate the existing manuscript.

**Contributions.**

1. A claim-grade two-model workload-shape corpus; falsified if cells fail admission, floor transport, or custody.
2. A preregistered additive energy model; successful only if both held-out prediction intervals satisfy a frozen engineering tolerance.
3. A calibrated interaction test: residuals above the operative floor reject additivity rather than being explained away.
4. A refusal-aware energy-budgeting method that labels predictions outside the measured grid unsupported.

**Experiment plan.** The grid is 24 cells, normally `n=5`, with `n=10` only for cells prospectively identified as near-floor; approximately **120–160 science bundles**. Historical diagnostics suggest strong margins: 1.5B prefill rises from about 1.65 J at 128 tokens to 51.07 J at 4096, a **49 J diagnostic difference**; 64→512 decode is projected at roughly **40 J for 1.5B** and **~165 J for 7B**—both uncertain projections, but far above 5 J. The important unknown is the interaction/holdout residual, which may be below 5 J. That outcome means “additive at this instrument’s resolution,” not mathematical exactness. New capabilities: deterministic grid generation, held-out analysis, and multi-magnitude null-floor extraction. All runs remain sequential single requests.

**Hardware, venue, risks, goals.** Owned M3 Max only; no wall meter. Kill before a night if dry-run timing cannot fit 60 bundles plus operations and 20% margin, or if a predeclared floor cannot cover the grid. This is the strongest **ICPE full-paper** direction: ICPE explicitly includes performance measurement, modeling, benchmark design, and energy efficiency, although its 2027 research-track details remain TBA. [ICPE scope](https://icpe.spec.org/) [ICPE 2027 track](https://icpe2027.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/) It reuses `draft-v1.md` §§3–5 nearly verbatim and replaces §7 with predictive evaluation. It serves Ed’s modular-harness and energy-as-third-axis goals, though not a particular inference mechanism.

---

## 2. Cache Once, Pay Once? A Calibrated Prefix-Reuse Crossover

**Thesis.** On one pinned MLX stack, serialized prefix reuse has a measurable request-count and prompt-length crossover where cache construction plus repeated cache-assisted decoding becomes cheaper than repeated prefill.

**Project brief and steps.** Complete the D-117 three-window spine first; its 1.5B prefill/decode floors and prospective bundles supply the instrument characterization and uncached baseline. This direction then promotes the existing `replay_supported` feasibility result—fresh-process cache replay at 1,024 and 2,048 tokens, exact 64/64 output-token identity, cache-size prediction within 0.02%—into claim-grade energy science. Desk work must convert the spike into normal hash-bound bundles, put cache load inside the measured request boundary, record cache construction/save separately, freeze exact output identity, and preregister the crossover equation. Collect **two additional quiet windows**, then solve  
`E_build+save + k·E_cached < k·E_cold`.

**Contributions.**

1. A falsifiable energy crossover over prompt lengths 1,024, 2,048, and 4,096.
2. Direct separation of one-time cache construction from per-reuse request energy.
3. Exact-token evidence showing the contrasted decode output is identical.
4. A refusal rule for cache-load or save components too small to resolve independently.

**Experiment plan.** For each length: five cold-versus-cached ABBA blocks (**60 contrast members total**), five identical-path null blocks (**60 members**), and five build/save absolute repetitions; roughly **135 members**, split across two windows. Decode remains 64 greedy tokens. Proportional projections from the clean 4,096-token diagnostic imply avoidable prefill energy of approximately **12.8, 25.5, and 51.1 J** at the three lengths; these are uncertain sizing estimates, not claims. The recorded cache-load time was only ~0.4 ms and save time 14–28 ms, so their standalone energy may not clear 5 J. That is acceptable: the primary gross cold-versus-cached request contrast should clear, while tiny subcomponents may be reported unresolved. A failed contrast would show that saved compute is offset by state handling or altered execution—not that caching costs zero.

**Hardware, venue, risks, goals.** Owned M3 Max and existing MLX artifacts; no wall meter. The extension remains single-request: each bundle contains one cold or one cache-assisted request, with no concurrency or batching. Kill before collection if current MLX replay loses exact token identity, cache identity cannot be custody-bound, or a short governed pilot projects less than ~8 J at 1,024 tokens. Best fit: capstone chapter followed by ICPE Emerging/EuroMLSys; full ICPE becomes plausible with the full crossover and reproducible artifact. It reuses the MVP’s calibration, floors, protocol, and D-117 model data, while adding one mechanism section. This directly serves Ed’s KV/cache-variant and mechanism-level energy goals.

---

## 3. Two Boundaries, One Verdict: Validating `powermetrics` Against Wall Power

**Thesis.** Paired SoC-counter and AC-wall measurements can determine whether workload comparisons retain their magnitude and direction across measurement boundaries, while explicitly leaving phase attribution to the pulse calibration.

**Project brief and steps.** The D-117 windows first establish claim-grade phase floors and the 1.5B-versus-7B decode result under `powermetrics`. This paper then asks the reviewer’s inevitable question: does the named software boundary track physical input energy? Borrow the advisor lab’s calibrated Yokogawa WT310E, build the already-designed external-meter importer and synchronization path, run a daytime non-claim pilot, freeze the bridge only after observing meter cadence and load-specific uncertainty, then collect one pilot/design-input and one confirmatory claim window. The wall leg reruns D-117 anchor workloads; it does not attempt to retrofit wall data onto earlier traces.

**Contributions.**

1. A paired `powermetrics`-to-wall regression with held-out residuals; rejected if synchronization or residual gates fail.
2. A boundary-sensitivity test for the 1.5B-versus-7B ordering.
3. Evidence distinguishing absolute-scale validation from phase-attribution validation.
4. A reusable, refusal-capable external-meter artifact format.

**Experiment plan.** Use five simultaneous paired blocks for four active levels: calibration pulse load, 1.5B 128/512, 1.5B 4096/64, and 7B 128/512; reserve one workload family as the held-out bridge test. Include battery-neutralized idle references and ABBA-like order. Historical internal energies span roughly **47 J to ~200 J**, so the workloads themselves are comfortably measurable. The actual wall-minus-SoC residual is unknown and may be **below 5 J**. The existing ~5 J phase-contrast sizing bar does not automatically govern the external meter; a new paired meter/synchronization floor does. A sub-floor residual permits only “no boundary difference resolved,” never equivalence. New capabilities are external trace import, clock alignment, meter metadata, paired reduction, and boundary calibration. Simultaneous telemetry does not alter the single-request boundary.

**Hardware, venue, risks, goals.** Owned M3 Max plus a **borrowed, in-calibration WT310E; wall meter dependency: yes**. No new compute hardware. Kill before the claim window if the unit lacks calibration status, a safe inline fixture, exportable timestamps, battery-charge neutralization, or a synchronization bound tight enough for the target residuals. This is the strongest pure-metrology extension for ICPE and also fits HotCarbon’s sustainable-AI and measurement scope. [HotCarbon scope](https://hotcarbon.org/cfp) It reuses virtually all MVP method prose and adds external-scale validation, paired-boundary results, and sharper limitations. It does not test speculative decoding, MoE, MTP, or KV mechanisms; it instead enables Ed’s energy-honest reporting and future cross-boundary leaderboard critique.
